title: One score, a live rating and calmer pages
summary: Every score is out of 100, the live rating can show while you play, and updates wait in the bar.

items.text: One score: every grade is out of 100 with no letters, and the match rating is shown out of 100 too, so 8.3 now reads 83.
The live rating can show on the Recording screen while you play. It stays off until you turn it on beside Start or in Settings.
Start takes you straight to the Recording screen, and every animation in the app holds still while a match records.
Updates download in the background and wait in a green button at the top right, so you restart when it suits you.
Home: your last match is one card you can click, each repeated mistake shows whether it is getting better or worse, and the moon is the real Moon, slowly turning.
Your rank card shows your tier's own icon and how much RR you need for the next rank.
Matches: simpler rows, your grade across the top, delete a match with its clips, and once you have played enough, the best and worst times of day for you to play.
The review plays your best highlight at the top, shows what moved your rating in every round, and Replay rating can pause and step through each moment.
Clips: your best clip at the top, filters by map, agent and more, delete a clip, open it in its folder, and see how much space clips take.
Practice is calmer and grouped into Mechanics, Game sense and Awareness.
Your mouse side buttons go back and forward between pages, and a back arrow on a review takes you where you came from.
Reviews and Ask Coach know the spike's plant and defuse times again, a clutch only counts when you survived the round, and one mistake always has one name.

title: A new moon
summary: Occlara has a new logo, a full moon in the night sky, and a calmer loading screen.

items.text: A new logo: a full moon with its seas and craters, lit from the upper left and falling to indigo, on the app icon, in the top bar and on the Recording screen.
The loading screen is one calm motion: the moon comes out of the night, then the name fades in beneath it.
The tray icon shows the moon, and while a match records it turns into the same ring and dot as the Start button.

title: A new look
summary: Occlara has a whole new look, calmer and smoother, with your fix for next match first.

items.text: A new design across the app: a night sky with the moon over Home, your agent standing in front of it, and calmer pages that each lead with one thing.
Home leads with your fix for next match, then your last match, your grade over your last four matches and what keeps costing you.
Four places instead of eight: Home, Matches, Practice and Clips. Patterns and Stats live inside Matches, the aim Trainer inside Practice, and Ask Coach opens from a review or the profile menu.
Review ready: when a review is done, a card drops in and opens into it while your grade counts up.
Your agent's full portrait on Home and at the top of every review.
Medals on the review for things you really did, such as your best grade in your last four matches.
Clips leads with the best moments of your newest match, then shows every death and highlight as a frame you can filter, with a still from each clip that was kept.
Start is the clearest button in the app, with a record icon beside the word, and buttons, pages and sheets move more smoothly.
The Recording screen is quieter: the time, map, agent, score, round and round tape, and nothing on it pulses.
A new app icon: the crescent in glass on a night sky.

title: Match rating
summary: Every match Riot confirms now gets a rating out of 10 that moves with each kill, death, plant and defuse.

items.text: Match rating: a number from 0.0 to 10.0 that starts at 6.0. Every move is how much your action changed your team's chance to win the round, so an opening kill counts for more than the last kill of a 5v1.
Replay the rating: watch the number rise and fall through the match, event by event, ending on your full time rating and your place in the lobby.
The line across the match, with the rounds that moved your rating most and what happened in each, such as a quadra kill, a won clutch, or dying first with nobody to trade.
A traded death costs less than an untraded one, kills after the round is decided count for almost nothing, and a round Riot marked you AFK in moves nothing.

title: Occlara Duos, on the way
summary: This update carries Occlara Duos, which switches on soon with no further update needed.

items.text: Occlara Duos: add a friend who uses Occlara, and after each match you play together on one team you both see, round by round, where each of you died and what each of you was doing.
Watch both clips of a round side by side on one clock, and leave your duo a pin on a moment of their clip, picked from a short list.
A duo needs a Max plan on one side. The other player can join with any plan, or none. Clips for shared matches upload by themselves after the match and are deleted after 30 days.
Nothing uploads or downloads while you are in a match, and you can block or report anyone, which ends the duo and removes what was shared.

title: Player profiles and search, on the way
summary: This update carries public profiles and a Players page, which switch on soon with no further update needed.

items.text: Public profiles: pick a username and choose whether other Occlara players can find you. Your profile shows your rank, average grade, record, main agents and maps, and recent matches.
A Players page to search for other Occlara players by username and open their profile. You can block or report a profile.
Profiles are off until you turn yours on, and can be turned off again at any time. Your email, your mistakes and anything you typed are never shown to anyone.

title: Occlara Wrapped is coming
summary: Occlara now keeps a record of your whole year, and from 15 December it plays it back as an animated story.

items.text: Occlara Wrapped: an animated story of your year. Your matches and hours, main agent and map, how your grade moved, your best match, your highlights, the mistake you beat and a player title.
Wrapped ends on a card you can save or copy as an image. It opens from 15 December to 31 January, from Home and from Profile.

Occlara now keeps one small record per reviewed match for the whole year, so your January still counts in December. It is filled in from the reviews already on your PC, stays on your PC, and holds no names.
Wrapped never opens or plays during a match, and it has a mute button and a calmer version when Windows is set to reduce motion.

title: Your highlights are clipped now
summary: Every multi kill and won clutch gets its own clip after the match, with the dead time between kills cut out.

items.text: Every 2K, 3K, 4K, ace and won clutch now gets a clip after the match. Before this, only your deaths were clipped, so a 3K showed on Moments with no video.

When the kills are far apart, the waiting between them is cut out and the pieces are joined into one clip. The player marks each kill and each cut on the timeline, and tells you how many seconds were skipped as you pass a cut.
Moments has a Highlights reel that plays all of your highlight clips back to back.
Imported recordings get highlight clips too.

title: No more antivirus alert on the capture helper
summary: Bitdefender flagged a small Occlara file by mistake, and that file is no longer part of the app.

items.text: Bitdefender and NETGEAR Armor quarantined OcclaraCapture.exe as a trojan. It was a false alarm on a tiny helper that took the screenshot Occlara reads, and the app no longer ships that file.
The screenshot is now taken by ffmpeg, the open source video tool Occlara already includes, in the same way as before. Nothing reads game memory or touches game files.

title: A Trainer closer to the game
summary: The Trainer was checked number by number against another Valorant trainer and the game, and now aims, sprays and stops closer to it.

items.text: Aiming down sights now zooms the view the way the game does, and rifles fire a little slower while aimed, as in the game.
Each gun's spray opens bullet by bullet the way the game does, climbs and levels off, and rifles drift to one side before they can switch.
Stopping takes the time Riot measured for every weapon, and walking or running error now applies in full as soon as you move that fast.
Shots land closer to the middle of the crosshair when you stand still or walk, and spread evenly when you run or jump.
After a run, a graph shows every shot you fired, split into firing error and movement error.
Bots slow down when you hit them, and the strafing targets now move left and right unpredictably, with short taps.

title: Fight your deaths again
summary: Replay a death from your review in the Trainer, which has a new look, real models and two new arenas.

items.text: Fight it again: a death in your review gets a button that rebuilds that fight in the Trainer, from what Riot recorded of it. You get five tries at it.
The Trainer lists your recent deaths under Your deaths and tells you when your last match has new ones to fight.
Matches reviewed from now on keep how far away your killer was, so the fight is set at the real range. Older reviews judge the range from the weapon.
The Trainer has a new night look, with a real rifle, pistols, a knife and hands, and bots that aim, run and fall.
Two new arenas: clearing a close corner, and holding a site after the plant.
Weapon and ability icons beside what killed you in reviews and Moments, and beside your most used weapon on your Profile.

title: The Trainer
summary: An aim and movement trainer inside Occlara, with your own sensitivity and the game's movement and accuracy rules.

items.text: A new Trainer tab with aim drills on a range and three arenas: retaking a site, holding a long main and peeking on two levels.
Type your sensitivity and DPI and the view turns as it does in the game, with raw mouse input. The Calibration drill lets you check it against the game's own Range.

Run speeds, the accuracy rule for moving, first shot accuracy, fire rates, reloads, armour and damage use the game's own numbers. Recoil and a few movement values are measured or estimated, and the Trainer says how many.
Hard levels have bots that shoot back, armour and a time limit. On Easy they never shoot.
Every run ends on a report with your score, accuracy, headshots, first bullet hits, reaction, time to kill and stop time, a chart of your last runs and your best.
Use your own crosshair from a pasted crosshair code or the sliders, and set your keys, the target outline colour and the volume.
Some Practice drills have a Train this button that opens the matching drill in the Trainer.
The Trainer is free and uses no games. It runs on your PC, sends nothing anywhere and is locked during a match like every page.

title: Flag a death, and go deeper on any death
summary: Press a key after a death you want to study, and ask the coach to explain any death further.

items.text: Press F8 after a death in a Valorant match to flag it. You hear one quiet tick, and you can change the key in Settings.
A flagged death gets a longer clip that the storage limit never removes, a yellow flag on its round and a line under your stats.
Further explain on any death asks the coach what happened, why it went wrong and what to do instead. Flagged deaths get this by themselves.

title: Import a recording
summary: Pro and Max players can add a video of a match they already have and get the same review as a live one.

items.text: Import a recording from Matches: an mp4, mkv, mov or webm of up to about an hour becomes a full review, with your deaths, stills and clips.
Pick the match from Riot's recent list to check it against Riot's record. An older video is reviewed from the screen, without a grade, and says so.
Pro includes 5 imports a month and Max has no monthly limit. Each import uses 1 game, and is given back if it fails.
Delete an imported match from its row in Matches. Its review, clips and frames go, and your video file stays where it is.

title: Practice shows the round you are fixing
summary: Each focus on the Practice page now shows your own clip of that mistake, and Occlara is locked down further after a full security review.

items.text: Practice shows your newest recorded clip of each mistake beside its drills. Press Watch the round to see exactly what went wrong.
Drills can now carry a short demo video, so you can see how to do them. The first ones arrive over the next updates.
A security review of the app and the server found no backdoors. The installed app now refuses developer switches and debugging tools, checks its own files, and only lets its own pages talk to it.
Plans and games are only granted once a payment has actually gone through, and the server refuses more kinds of misuse.

title: Gifts and upgrades get their moment
summary: When games or a plan reach you, a centred animation shows exactly what you got, instead of a small note in the corner.

items.text: A gift, an invite that paid off, games you bought or a higher free allowance now open a gift on screen and count up the games you got.
Upgrading to Pro or Max draws a ring around the crescent and counts up your games a month, in gold for Max.
Continue, Esc or a click outside closes it, See my games opens your Profile, and it waits until your match is over.

title: Fixes that fit the round
summary: Each fix now fits your side and your level, aim gets counted, and every top mistake has a target for next match.

items.text: Shots landing below the head is a new repeated mistake, counted from your hits in Riot's record against what is usual at your rank, with aim drills on the Practice page.
Under the top mistake's fix, a target for the next match: how many rounds it happened in, and at how few it goes away.
Fixes now fit the side you died on: a retake is told to go onto the spike together, a defender holding alone is told to take one look and fall back, and a defence death is never treated as an entry.
One mistake with many rounds no longer pushes every other one off the top, so the card you see first changes with what really cost you the match.
Reviews below Platinum keep to 4 round lines, and each line says what the enemy could do, not only what happened.
Practice this opens the drills for the mistake the review's focus is about, and drill goals are counts you can beat rather than results the enemy decides.
A whole site like B Site no longer counts as a spot you keep dying at, and No ability used is no longer blamed on a defender holding utility early in the round.
Pressing Start with the game closed is now always cancelled after 5 minutes, even if one read of the screen came back unclear.
The live status switches on the Recording screen and in Settings now always show the same thing.
Bought and invite games are now called bonus games, and yearly plans show what they save.

title: Advice that fits the map
summary: On Bind, Fracture and Lotus the coach never draws on advice about mid, so answers stay whole.

items.text: On Bind, Fracture and Lotus, which have no mid, the coach no longer uses advice about taking or watching mid, in reviews or in Ask Coach.

title: Ask Coach keeps more of what is true
summary: Ask Coach stops cutting true sentences out of its answers, and drops a few more wrong ones.

items.text: Ask Coach keeps true sentences it used to cut: numbers you gave it yourself, the working behind a damage answer, kit rules like a reset every two kills, and advice phrased as how to win more fights like a round you lost.
A short, correct answer to a direct question is shown as it is, without being asked again.
Ask Coach no longer talks about mid on Bind, Fracture or Lotus, and drops advice that gets the spike, the defuse or a reload you never did wrong.

title: Practice, and reviews that read the whole match
summary: A new Practice page built from your own repeated mistakes, and reviews that name every mistake in a death and remember the match.

items.text: Practice: a plan built from your own repeated mistakes, with drills for your rank, a goal for each, and a plain check on whether the mistake is going away. Mark drills as practiced and see your streak.
Reviews read a death as a chain: the first mistake, what made it worse, and what happened earlier in the match, like dying at the same spot or to the same enemy again.
Ask Coach and your review now remember the match, so they can say you died here twice before, or that an enemy started finding you from a round on.
Home suggests today's practice, and each review has a Practice this link under its fix.
More researched coaching advice, including holding the power on defence before the plant.

title: Ask Coach keeps its whole answer
summary: Ask Coach no longer loses true sentences mid answer, and drops a few more claims it cannot back up.

items.text: Ask Coach no longer cuts true sentences out of an answer when you mention CT or a wait like 1 to 1.5 seconds, so answers no longer have a hole in the middle.
Ask Coach drops claims that get the spike timing backwards, that a drone flies on its own, or that a Sheriff head hit kills at long range, and never mentions its own notes.

title: Reviews read defence deaths right
summary: A death on defence is never called an entry, a risky spot with no way out has its own cause, and the coach checks more of what it says.

items.text: A death on defence is never called an entry. Reviews keep entry advice for attack.
A new death cause, Risky spot, no escape: you got a kill and the next enemy killed you a second later, too soon to leave. Its fix tells you to hold from a spot you can step back from.
Ask Coach no longer guesses which site the enemy will hit next. It tells you what to look and listen for instead, and gives better advice on taking mid and playing too passive.

Ask Coach answers how many body shots a gun needs through armour again, and drops claims about guided darts, long range head shots, utility used for the wrong side, and praise for things you did not do.

title: Lighter recording
summary: Recording costs your PC less while you play, and the clips stay at 30 fps.

items.text: Recording is lighter on your PC: the screen is captured at 45 frames a second instead of 60, while your clips stay at 30.
Before a match, the check for whether the game is open costs a fraction of what it did.
Settings and setup now suggest turning off NVIDIA Instant Replay, AMD ReLive or Xbox Game Bar capture while Occlara records, for the smoothest game.

title: Stay signed in, and a Start with no game stops by itself
summary: You stay signed in after closing the app, a Start with no game ends itself, and the coach is more careful.

items.text: You stay signed in when you close and reopen Occlara. Since 8.9.1 it asked you to sign in again at every launch.
If you press Start and never get into a game, Occlara stops watching by itself: after 5 minutes with Valorant closed, or 30 minutes in the menus. Nothing is counted and no game is used.

Ask Coach gives better advice on trading teammates after the plant and on pushing through your own smoke, and drops claims about head shots at long range, the clock before the plant and shooting on the move.
Opening the account menu with the keyboard puts you on its first row.

title: The coach sticks to what it gets right
summary: The coach no longer gives economy advice, and it drops claims it cannot back up.

items.text: The coach no longer covers the economy. Reviews and Ask Coach stop giving buy, save and money advice, and an economy question gets a plain answer that it is not covered.
Ask Coach drops claims it cannot back up: a won pistol round nobody mentioned, habits stated about a whole map, and a Marshal body shot that only kills an unarmoured player.
Better advice on map control and on reading where the enemy will go next.
The Recording screen says no tips or advice until the match ends, since it now shows your map, agent, score and round.

title: More motion, and chart numbers that stay off the line
summary: The app moves with more care, and the numbers on your grade charts no longer sit on the line.

items.text: The app has more motion: the tab marker glides between pages, numbers count up, lines draw themselves, bars grow, and pages and lists rise in once when you open them. Reduced motion in Windows turns all of it off.
Buttons press in when you click them, and switches slide between choices.
The numbers on your grade charts on Home and Matches no longer sit on the line.

title: Four free games, and a note when games arrive
summary: Free is now 4 games, everyone gets 2 more, and a card tells you when a gift or new games arrive.

items.text: Free is now 4 games for life, 6 with an invite. Every account gets 2 more, including players who already used theirs.
When someone sends you a gift, an invite pays off or new games arrive, a card slides in to tell you. It waits until your match ends.
Your account menu opens as a dropdown from your avatar, over the page.
Home shows your Riot ID, the K/D of your last match, and plays the fix clip right there.
Stats shows more of your numbers: combat score, K/D and damage a round, where your shots land, your maps and your acts.
The Patterns chart is easier to read: one colour, lines for each grade letter, your average, and whether your last match was above or below it.
Recording keeps the AI log on, because the review needs those frames to look at your deaths. Turning recording off now asks first.
The times under the Matches chart no longer run together, and the wins and losses count is gone.

title: A new look, and a live status while you play
summary: A new look with a top bar, and a live status of your Valorant match on the Recording screen.

items.text: A new look across the app. The sidebar is replaced by a top bar with your pages, the game switch and your account menu, and Home, Matches, reviews and Settings are redrawn.

While a Valorant match is on, the Recording screen shows its map, your agent, the score and the round, with a strip that draws the rounds as they go. Each one has a switch in Settings, and nothing else about the match is shown until it ends.
Maps have their own art on Home and in reviews.
Ask Coach no longer drops a correct answer about how many hits a gun needs to kill through armor.
With no match attached, Ask Coach reads the round you describe and picks advice that fits it far more often.

title: The previous look is back, and the coach checks more of what it says
summary: The app looks the way it did before 8.8.0, and reviews and Ask Coach check six more kinds of claim against Riot's record.

items.text: The app is back to its previous look. The notebook redesign from 8.8.0 is gone.

Reviews and Ask Coach now check six more kinds of claim against Riot's record: where you died, which rounds the coach looked at and how many, whether you died more than you killed, lists of rounds that do not match their count, and utility your team does not have, like a drone.
Ask Coach gives better advice on holding an angle with a sniper, buying on pistol, eco and team save rounds, retakes and defusing, and reading which site the enemy will hit next.
With no match attached, Ask Coach no longer talks about what a record shows.

title: A coach's notebook, and fewer wrong claims
summary: The app looks like a coach's marked up notes, and reviews check what they say about your rounds more strictly.

items.text: Review, Home and Matches are redesigned like a coach's notebook, with the one thing to fix in bold, hand drawn pen marks on the rounds that prove it and a margin for times and grades.
Buttons now have three clear ranks, one main action per screen, and press down a little when you click them.
Counts in reviews and Ask Coach, like how many deaths nobody traded, now come from one list, so they no longer contradict each other or call a death alone when Riot shows a teammate close.
A round where Riot marked you AFK is now left out of your grade, your missed list, your patterns and your Moments, not only your repeated mistakes.
Ask Coach answers aim questions from your own numbers with drills you can really do, and the RR on your reviews keeps trying until Riot publishes the game.
A review no longer loses its round lines when a player in your match has a name that contains a word like aim.

title: Where you died, and what you bought
summary: Linked round cards now show where each death happened, what your team bought and how close a teammate was.

items.text: When your match is linked to Riot's record, each round you died in shows the spot, like B Main, and whether a teammate was close enough to trade you.
Each linked round shows your team's buy, from pistol to full buy, and longer matches count how your team did on full buys, ecos and forced buys.
Reviews of your recent ranked matches show the RR you gained or lost, and Stats adds your peak rank and your all time aces and clutches from Riot's record.
The coach picks advice from where you died and how you bought, and a round where Riot marked you AFK says so on its card and is left out of your repeated mistakes.

Reviews and Ask Coach check what they say about a round, where you died, the plant and how close a teammate was, against Riot's record, so fewer mistakes reach you, and higher ranks get advice that fits them.
Reviews saved before this update look exactly as before.

title: A coach that reads your match, not a checklist
summary: Reviews and answers now lean on what your match and your own history show, with sharper advice at every rank.

items.text: Reviews pick the lesson that fits your rank and your match, and only lead with trading when it keeps costing you across your matches.
Higher ranks get advice built on their match's real numbers, like a side that kept losing or a post plant that kept failing.
Ask Coach answers practice, aim and improvement questions with your own biggest lever instead of the same habit every time.
The coach no longer gets agent abilities wrong, quotes stats it cannot check, or leaves half sentences behind.

title: Sharper, more honest coaching
summary: Reviews and Ask Coach now focus on what really decided your match, answer the question you asked, and check their facts harder.

items.text: Your review now leads with the change that would help you most, like a side you kept losing or a player who kept killing you, not the same habit every time.
Ask Coach answers what you asked: aim, practice, climbing or how to play into an agent, with notes picked for that question.
Aim is judged from your own numbers, and a death in a round you lost is no longer praised just because it was traded.
Advice at higher ranks goes deeper than advice at lower ranks, not just longer.
The coach no longer mixes up ability keys or makes up details the match record does not show, and it answers basic questions it used to refuse.

title: A coach that knows the matchup
summary: More coaching from top players, advice that knows who you played against, and worked examples for the moments that decided your match.

items.text: The coach learned 133 more habits from top coaches and Radiant players, with much more for Ascendant and above.
Matchup advice: when the enemy had a Killjoy, a Viper or another agent that changes how you play, the coach tells you how to play into them.
When a moment in your match looks like one top players handle well, the coach walks you through what to notice and what to do.
Lower ranks now get the fundamentals that matter most at their level first, while higher ranks keep the deeper advice.

title: Report a problem, and advanced coaching for everyone
summary: Tell us when something goes wrong with a picture and a few words, and get the deepest coaching that fits your rank by default.

items.text: A Report a problem button above the Discord icon. Describe what went wrong, add up to 3 pictures and send it straight to us.
Advanced coaching is now on for everyone. It goes deeper while fitting your rank, so you never get advice meant for a rank above yours. You can still turn it off in Settings.
Ask Coach no longer tells you your rank back, it just fits its advice to it.

title: Gifts, clips in Ask Coach and a smarter coach
summary: Gift Pro or Max to a friend with a link, watch your own clips inside Ask Coach, and get advice that fits your rank.

items.text: Gift Pro or Max for a month or a year. You get a link to send, and your friend redeems it in one click.
Ask Coach can show the clips it is talking about, right under its answer.
Each round you died in shows who killed you, with their agent, weapon and the damage they did.
A Discord button in the sidebar and a What's new page in Settings.
The coach learned from top coaches and Radiant players, and its advice now fits your rank.
Your Verdict shows your agent and your standout stat of the match, like an ace or a clutch.
Rounds are cleaner, without the row of small frames under each clip.
Free games are now one set per player.

title: Ask Coach and your games
summary: Ask Coach now follows your games, with a clear way to get more when you run out.

items.text: When you have used all your games, Ask Coach says so in one calm line with a button that opens your Profile.
Games you buy unlock Ask Coach straight away.
Ask Coach takes one question at a time and slows down questions sent very fast.
Reviews and Ask Coach answers come from newer AI models that matched the old ones in our tests and cost less to run.
Occlara's servers now guard every request against floods, so the coach stays up for everyone.

title: Your Profile, and buying games
summary: A new Profile page shows your games left, lets you buy more and sums up how you play.

items.text: A Profile page in the sidebar, between Invite and Settings, with your games left as the first thing you see.
Buy more games from the app at $2 a game, any number from 1 to 500. Games you buy never expire.
Your play in Valorant at a glance: your most used weapon, your most played agent and your peak rank.
The Free, Pro and Max plans side by side, monthly or yearly.
The coach's notes were checked and corrected, and it reads the latest patch notes again.
A chosen option in a switch no longer turns invisible when you hover it.
Your match library rebuilds itself if its index is ever damaged, so no review is lost.
A revive no longer counts as a clutch.
Spike Rush matches are read correctly, halves included.
A round end countdown is no longer mistaken for a death.
An update never restarts Occlara in the middle of a match.
Round pictures in a review show again instead of a broken image.

title: Highlights for every multikill
summary: Every round with two or more kills is now a highlight, and reviews read in plainer sentences.

items.text: Every round where you get two or more kills is saved as a highlight, named 2K, 3K, 4K or 5K, alongside clutches and first kill streaks.
Reviews are written in short plain sentences, without semicolons.

title: Accounts, a new look and Moments
summary: Sign in with your browser, start with 2 free games, and meet a calmer Occlara with the new Moments page.

items.text: Accounts: sign in through your browser. A licence key still works too.
Free, Pro and Max plans. Free gives you 2 games for life, Pro 25 games a month and Max 70 a month.
An Invite page. Each friend who signs up with your link gets 2 extra free games, and you earn 4 games per friend, up to 20.
Moments replaces Breakdown: every death and highlight from your matches in one place, with Play all for each repeated mistake.
A new look across the whole app: one calm column, clean lines instead of boxes, and the fix for your next match as the biggest line.
A lighter 480p recording size for modest PCs, which used about a quarter less CPU than 720p in our tests.
Reviews open with a Verdict you can share as an image, and show how you did against your last match and your average.
Milestones on Home and in Matches mark your bests and the habits you have cleared.
A match played with no games left is still saved in your library with Riot's record of it.
Invited friends get their extra games even if they confirm their email later.
League of Legends is marked coming soon while we finish it. Your League reviews are kept.

title: The crescent
summary: A new crescent mark and one cleaner look across the app.

items.text: A new crescent logo, with tray icons for light and dark taskbars.
Matches, Stats, Settings and reviews share one cleaner look.
The close button in the first run setup sits inside its card again.
